summary.headline: IOB posted record Q1 FY27 net profit of INR 1,659 crore, up 49.32% YoY, with GNPA at 1.33% and CASA ratio at 41.45%.
summary.overview: Indian Overseas Bank reported an all-time high quarterly net profit of INR 1,659 crore for Q1 FY27, against INR 1,111 crore a year earlier, with operating profit up 14.21% YoY to INR 2,693 crore. Business mix reached INR 6,98,325 crore (up 17.72% YoY) and advances grew 22.75% YoY to INR 3,22,132 crore. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.33% and slippage ratio at 0.06%. Management flagged that about INR 863 crore of PSLC commission and about INR 490 crore of technical write-off recoveries supported profit, and said these are recurring. Corporate loans fell about 10% QoQ after the bank exited a roughly INR 10,000 crore account on pricing grounds.

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,54,415 crore; domestic CASA ratio 41.45%, global 41.05%

financial_highlights.change: Global +12 bps QoQ from 3.25%; domestic from 3.35%
GNPA -64 bps YoY; NNPA -14 bps YoY
vs INR 28,114 crore in prior quarter
from INR 5,178 crore / INR 816 crore YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Fee-type income (normal exchange, LC/BG, locker, DD etc.)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR 398 crore a year earlier (about +20%)

segments.name: Retail, agriculture and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM is about 80% of the advances book per management, with roughly 40% of the book in agriculture general loans. Management reported no stress in agriculture or small-borrower/SME accounts linked to the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate loans fell about 10% QoQ after the bank exited a roughly INR 10,000 crore account in April on pricing grounds; about 40% of that exposure was covered in Q1. Pipeline of about INR 14,000 crore sanctioned; management targets 12-13% corporate book growth by year-end.

segments.name: International / GIFT City
segments.commentary: IFSCA licence for a GIFT City branch received about 3-4 months ago; branch expected to be operational in about 2 months with an internal target book of USD 500 million by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guided at 13-14% for FY27, described as a minimum; management says the bank has grown about 20-22% in recent years.
NIM expected to stay in the 3.3-3.4% range; domestic NIM was 3.48% in June.
ROA expected at about 1.4-1.5% over the next two to three quarters; around 1.46% targeted by year-end; internal floor of 1.20%.
Full-year credit cost guided at 0.35-0.40% against 0.14% in Q1.

ECL: internal estimate of about INR 3,000 crore additional requirement; INR 2,150 crore provided so far; the rest to be provided by year-end. Bank does not intend to use the four-year spread dispensation.
ECLGS: INR 4,400 crore universe; about INR 2,600 crore disbursed; INR 1,800 crore expected over the next 1-1.5 months; 95-100% disbursement expected by August end or early September.
Equity raise of INR 5,000 crore approved by the Board; statutory approvals in progress; market access expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27 in one or more tranches depending on market conditions.
FCNR(B): about USD 300 million mobilised so far; target USD 600-650 million by September 2026 when the current scheme window ends.
Cost of deposits expected to stay at current levels; repricing of term deposits said to be complete (about 6 months ago); bulk deposits kept at 6-7% of total deposits.
capex_capacity: Network: over 3,522 branches, around 3,691 ATMs and 13,401 business correspondents; operations in Singapore, Hong Kong, Thailand and Sri Lanka.
GIFT City branch under IFSCA licence; expected to become physically operational in about 2 months.
Digital: around 96% of transactions digital; around 75% of customer onboarding digital; loan applications can be sanctioned within about 10 minutes, per management.
Capital adequacy ratio of 19.36% vs 11.50% requirement; accumulated losses reported as nil after netting profit and share premium.
demand_pricing: Yield on advances rose about 10 bps QoQ on pricing; 54% of the book is MCLR-linked and 37% RLLR-linked; management says the increase is spread across segments.
Cost of deposits fell about 10 bps QoQ, driven by CASA focus and retail term deposit growth of about 17%.
Management said it will not chase sub-7% corporate lending; it exited the INR 10,000 crore account because pricing did not match.
Total SMA stood at about INR 13,000 crore (4.05%), down about INR 2,200 crore QoQ; SMA-2 rose about INR 500 crore QoQ to INR 4,246 crore, which management said was mostly regularised.
Fee-type income grew about 20% YoY on a low base; PSLC commission and recoveries from technical write-offs are reported within miscellaneous income, which rose about 423% QoQ per an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is profitability given PSLC income and write-off recoveries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PSLC sales and technical write-off recoveries recur every quarter across the last 8-9 quarters and are part of non-interest income. It cited 34.30% YoY NII growth as the main driver and saw no challenge to maintaining profitability.

qa_highlights.question: ECLGS disbursement status and any West Asia stress on SME accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 2,600 crore of INR 4,400 crore ECLGS disbursed, with INR 1,800 crore expected in 1-1.5 months. No product or sector-level stress seen from West Asia; only individual cases.

qa_highlights.question: ECL buffer and provisioning approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal estimate of INR 3,000 crore requirement; INR 2,150 crore provided so far; the rest to be provided across coming quarters so the requirement is fully met by year-end. No use of the four-year dispensation.

qa_highlights.question: Net worth rise of INR 554 crore beyond profit, and SMA details?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 200 crore from DTA and about INR 300 crore from AFS mark-to-market. SMA-0 INR 5,733 crore, SMA-1 INR 3,068 crore, SMA-2 INR 4,246 crore; no government-guaranteed accounts; CGTMSE/CGFMU coverage on smaller accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the corporate book fall 10% QoQ and where is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The fall reflects the exit from a roughly INR 10,000 crore account in April on pricing grounds; about 40% covered in Q1. Corporate book targeted to grow 12-13% by year-end; total credit grew about 4% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Equity raise plan and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore approved; statutory approvals pending; expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27, possibly in more than one tranche depending on market conditions. Mode not specified beyond market raise.

qa_highlights.question: Why was credit growth guidance 13-14% when growth has been about 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 13-14% is a floor; growth has run around 20-22% for three years and it expects this to continue if conditions stay normal.

qa_highlights.question: Gold-backed agriculture loans and delinquencies?
qa_highlights.answer: No delinquencies seen in agriculture loans; gold-backed exposure not quantified, but agriculture general loans are about 40% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cost of funds above cost of deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds includes borrowing costs, so it can exceed cost of deposits; management said this is seen at many banks.

risks_watch: Sustainability of profit: PSLC commission (about INR 863 crore) and technical write-off recoveries (about INR 490 crore) drove Q1; management calls them recurring but they are non-core and lumpy, so track their level next quarter.
Credit cost step-up: Q1 credit cost was 0.14% against full-year guidance of 0.35-0.40%, and about INR 850 crore of the INR 3,000 crore ECL requirement is still to be provided by year-end.
SMA-2 rose about INR 500 crore QoQ to INR 4,246 crore; management says it is mostly regularised, so watch SMA-2 and slippages in Q2.

Corporate book fell about 10% QoQ after the exit of a roughly INR 10,000 crore account; about 40% of that exposure was covered in Q1, and the 12-13% growth target depends on converting the INR 14,000 crore pipeline.
Equity raise of INR 5,000 crore: statutory approvals pending, market access expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27 in one or more tranches; dilution and instrument (QIP/OFS/rights) not yet specified.
West Asia conflict: management says no product- or sector-level stress yet, but mentions individual cases; monitor SME and agriculture asset quality.
ECLGS: about INR 1,800 crore of the INR 4,400 crore universe still to be disbursed; FCNR(B) target of USD 600-650 million by September 2026 against about USD 300 million mobilised so far.
key_quotes: So, I do not see any challenge in maintaining this profitability.
These are routine activity. Every quarter, it happens.
And we are pretty sure that 95% to 100% of ECLGS disbursement will certainly take place by August end or September first week.
We do not want to do any loss-making business. It's very clear.
The consistency is the hallmark of IOB and going forward also I can assure you on behalf of the entire IOB team that the same type of consistency will be visible going forward also.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and consistently upbeat, stressing consistency, the 22% credit growth and the 1.46% ROA target by year-end. It was more cautious and vague on sustainability of non-core income (PSLC and recoveries), the corporate book decline and the exact timing and format of the equity raise.

adds.what: GIFT City branch under IFSCA licence (physical operations expected in ~2 months)

growth.why: Management guides credit growth of 13-14% for FY27 (described as a minimum, vs ~20-22% recent history), backed by a INR 14,000 crore corporate sanction pipeline, a 12-13% corporate book target, and FCNR(B) mobilisation targets; no new physical capacity beyond the GIFT City branch, and the 13-14% guide is only partly supported by concrete orders.
